 Xbox Offers Gamers a Doctor’s Note for the “Biggest Week in Gaming”
 Monday, 16 November 2026, 20:51 
 Photo source: IGN 
 Xbox’s new campaign hints at GTA 6 without naming it and lets players generate a note recommending time off to play games. 
 Microsoft is trying to build excitement among Xbox players for a game its marketing cannot name. The campaign follows the recent announcement of an alligator-shaped Xbox.
 This is reported by IGN .
 “Are you suffering from Vitamin G deficiency?” the campaign asks. “Dr. XBOX has you covered.” The copy leaves out vitamins T and A, too.
 Advertisement 
 For reasons left unexplained, Dr. Xbox is DJ Khalid, who wants to get players ready for “the biggest week in gaming.” The campaign does not explain what makes it the biggest week.
 The website lets visitors enter their name and receive a personalized doctor’s note recommending they play games on Xbox this week. DJ Khalid is not a medical professional, and gamer vitamins do not exist, so the note probably will not work on your boss.
 After I entered my details, the letter read: “As their physician, mentor, and professional motivator, I am prescribing the patient take some time off to enjoy the biggest week in gaming,” followed by, “I advise they avoid all meetings, highly stressful jobs, and unnecessary negativity.”
 It also lists possible symptoms: “twitchy thumbs, controller cramps or release-date restlessness.”
 The campaign does not say what makes this the biggest week in gaming. The article suggests that may be because Sony has an exclusive marketing deal with Rockstar to promote the game’s release on PlayStation.
 Xbox has previously had some notable omissions in its marketing. The first version of a GTA 6 TV spot did not mention that the game was coming to Xbox consoles.
 Microsoft later announced that GTA 6 would be playable through the cloud. That would let people who own only an Xbox One stream the game, with access to Xbox Series S graphics settings.
 What those Xbox Series S graphics settings mean is still unclear. Rockstar has said GTA 6 will run at 30fps on all platforms, while PS5 Pro will get some ray-tracing upgrades. There is no word on what compromises the studio had to make to run the game on Xbox Series S.
